meta.title: Total solar eclipse of 2 August 2027 in Spain: municipalities in the path of totality and historical clear-sky probability
meta.cite: Astroletra (2026). Eclipse total del 2 de agosto de 2027, municipios de la franja de totalidad y probabilidad histórica de cielo despejado (ERA5, 1991-2020). https://astroletra.com/eclipses/eclipse-solar-total-2-agosto-2027/mejores-sitios/

eclipse.ephemeris: JPL DE440 (NASA), Besselian elements computed by Astroletra, ΔT from IERS Bulletin A
eclipse.observer: centre of each municipality (GeoNames CC BY 4.0, Wikidata), on the ellipsoid, no lunar limb profile

clouds.dataset: ERA5 hourly data on single levels from 1940 to present (Copernicus Climate Change Service, ECMWF)
clouds.attribution: Contains modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information (2026). Neither the European Commission nor ECMWF is responsible for any use that may be made of the Copernicus information or data it contains.
clouds.method: Bilinear interpolation of the 0.25° grid to each municipality and linear interpolation between 08 and 09 UTC to the middle of its totality.

meta.score: expected_totality_s = totality_duration_s × clear_sky_probability (seconds of totality you can expect to see), rounded; expected_totality_margin95_s = 1.96 × totality_duration_s × clear_sky_probability_se (95% margin, years as blocks).
meta.tied_with_first: true when the difference in expected seconds with rank 1, computed year by year over the same 30 summers (paired), is below 2.045 standard errors (95%, Student t with 29 degrees of freedom): those municipalities cannot be told apart from the first.
meta.caveat: Historical climatology, not a forecast. ERA5 cells are about 28 × 22 km and do not resolve local fog, sea breeze clouds or relief. Durations are for the centre of each municipality, without the lunar limb profile; near the edges of the path (under about 30 s) totality may not happen at all. Start, end and duration are each rounded to the second, so end minus start can differ from the duration by 1 s.
